question: Where can I get the capacity of the gas grid to receive biomethane injection in the United States, by zone or connection point?

answer.summary: No US source publishing grid hosting capacity for new biomethane injection by zone or point was found (federal, CPUC and 5 utilities checked). The closest official data are interstate pipeline informational postings (FERC 18 CFR 284.13): daily design, operating and operationally available capacity in MMBtu for existing RNG/biogas receipt points, e.g. Northern Natural Gas (15 points) and Florida Gas Transmission (5). Gas utilities (PG&E, SoCalGas, Con Edison, NW Natural) give takeaway capacity only in per-project screening or feasibility studies (non-binding under the California tariff); seasonal limits are noted but not published.
main_caveats: Interstate OAC describes existing receipt points only; it is not available capacity for a new plant and must not be read as hosting capacity.
The distribution utilities checked provide takeaway capacity through project-specific studies.
The public sources checked lack firm and seasonal capacity figures for new connections. Existing point postings vary by gas day and nomination cycle.
Do not infer capacity from plant output (EPA LMOP flows, CPUC injected therms) or from pipeline maps (NPMS, utility maps).
Seven interstate pipeline postings were checked. Two yielded capacity figures for existing biomethane receipt points.
answer.confidence_reason: Absence of published LDC capacity checked on 5 utilities in 4 states and in the CPUC tariff; interstate data tested on 2 pipelines with queries; SoCalGas/National Grid sites blocked and 176 pipelines unsampled.

attributes.gap_note: Earliest gas day served by each pipeline's API/CSV not determined; other 176 pipelines not checked.

sources.name: Interstate pipeline informational postings: operationally available capacity and location lists per receipt point
sources.publisher: FERC-regulated interstate natural gas pipelines, each on its own informational postings site
sources.format: JSON and CSV (Northern Natural Gas API); CSV/Excel/ODS/PDF/XML downloads (Energy Transfer ipost)
sources.adds: Only published, dated capacity per connection point found: design, operating, scheduled and operationally available capacity (MMBtu per gas day) for existing biogas/RNG receipt points, plus county/state from the pipeline's location list.
sources.summary: Daily point-level design, operating, scheduled and available capacity (MMBtu) for existing biogas/RNG receipt points on interstate pipelines.
sources.coverage_note: Only interstate pipelines and only points already built; NNG (15 biogas receipt points, Midwest) and FGT (5 RNG receipt points, Florida) confirmed; other pipelines sampled.
caveats: Capacity of an existing RNG meter point, not hosting capacity for new plants.
OAC is an estimate per gas day and cycle; delivery (D) rows at the same site are not injection.

coverage.geographic: Interstate transmission pipelines only (178 posting pipelines per FERC). Tested: Northern Natural Gas (15 biogas receipt points in IA, KS, MN, NE, SD, WI) and Florida Gas Transmission (5 RNG receipt points in FL).

unit.value: MMBtu per gas day (posted as 'Million BTU's' by Northern Natural Gas, 'MMBtu' by Florida Gas Transmission; CSV code 'BZ').

inclusion_rule.value: Every active receipt and delivery point with its design capacity must be posted; biomethane points are identifiable by location type (NNG Locations type 'BIO'; FGT OAC filter 'RNG - Renewable Natural Gas') or by point name.
inclusion_rule.quote: the availability of capacity at receipt points, on the mainline, at delivery points, and in storage fields, whether the capacity is available directly from the pipeline or through capacity release, the total design capacity of each point or segment on the system, the amount scheduled at each point or segment whenever capacity is scheduled

reference_date.value: Each posting is for one gas day and nomination cycle, with its own post timestamp; latest checked: gas day 2026-11-27, Timely cycle posted 2026-11-26 16:48 (NNG).
reference_date.quote: The Operationally Available Capacity posted is an estimate of the capacity which could be scheduled at or through the group or point in the indicated direction of flow for the Gas Day and cycle referenced.

update_frequency.value: Daily, per nomination cycle (NNG: Timely, Evening, Non-Grid A.M., Intraday 1-3, Final A.M.; FGT: Timely, Evening). FERC treats postings as at least daily.
update_frequency.quote: The interstate natural gas pipeline postings set an appropriate standard: postings should occur at least daily.

exclusions.value: Intrastate pipelines and local distribution (LDC) networks, where many RNG plants connect, are outside this obligation; values are estimates without guarantee; no firm vs seasonal split per point.
exclusions.quote: FERC-551 allows companies to fulfill the posting requirements by including the information on the companies' websites and does not require companies to file the information with the Commission.

attempts.note: NNG comment: 'there are no guarantees expressed or implied that these capacities will be available.'

key_fields.meaning: Pipeline location number of the point (stable key to join OAC with the Locations list).
Point name; biogas points carry names such as 'BIOGAS REC', 'RNG' or 'DAIRY'.
Pipeline zone of the point (e.g. NNG 'MID 17', FGT 'MARKET').
R = receipt (injection into the pipeline), D = delivery.
Design capacity of the point, MMBtu per gas day.
Capacity the pipeline can operate at the point that day/cycle.
Quantity already scheduled at the point (a flow, not a capacity).
Estimated capacity still schedulable at the point for that gas day and cycle.
NNG: Y when quantities are scheduled on an MPS Agreement at a receipt point.

key_fields.field: Loc Cnty, Loc St Abbrev, Loc Loctr (Locations list)
key_fields.meaning: County, state and (NNG) PLSS section-township-range of the point; no coordinates.

how_to_use.example_request: curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"gasDay":"2026-11-27","cycle":10,"searchType":"Location names containing the following string","searchString":"BIOGAS","locationType":"All location types","locationZone":"","pagination":{"pageNumber":1,"pageSize":500},"download":false}' "https://www.northernnaturalgas.com/wp-json/api/capacity/oac/report"
how_to_use.example_result: postDateTime 2026-11-26T16:48:03, gasDateTime 2026-11-27T09:00, totalCount 24; {location:79509, locationZone:'MID 17', locationName:'BRIGHTMARK ATHENA BALTIC BIOGAS REC', flowInd:'R', designCapacity:2832, operatingCapacity:2832, scheduledQuantity:500, availableCapacity:2332, interruptInd:'N'}
steps: Northern Natural Gas (member used in the example): list biogas points with POST https://www.northernnaturalgas.com/wp-json/api/locations and body {"searchType":"","pointStatus":"A","searchString":"","pointTypeNew":"BIO","groupName":"","zoneName":"","stateAbbreviation":"","pagination":{"pageNumber":1,"pageSize":100}} (15 active points on 2026-11-27, with county, state, PLSS locator, effective date and upstream party).

Query capacity with POST to /wp-json/api/capacity/oac/report: gasDay YYYY-MM-DD, cycle 10-16 (10 = Timely ... 16 = Final A.M.), searchType 'Location names containing the following string' and a string (BIOGAS, RNG, DAIRY) or 'A location with the following Loc (Location) number' with comma-separated Loc numbers. Add "download":true for a CSV (NNG_OperCap_YYYYMMDD.csv).

Florida Gas Transmission (Energy Transfer): GET the CSV with locType=RNG, searchType=ALL, cycle=0 (Timely) or 1 (Evening), gasDay=MM%2FDD%2FYYYY on https://peplmessenger.energytransfer.com/ipost/capacity/operationally-available?f=csv&extension=csv&asset=FGT...; join Loc with https://peplmessenger.energytransfer.com/ipost/locations/index?asset=FGT&f=csv&extension=csv for county and state.
Keep Flow Ind = R rows to measure receiving capacity; join to the Locations list on Loc; record the Effective Gas Day and Post Date/Time of each extract.
For history, repeat the query with an earlier gasDay: NNG returned data for 2020-11-27 and FGT for 2024-11-27, although the on-screen cycle grid of NNG lists only the last 90 gas days.
reading_traps: Biogas sites often have a paired delivery point (e.g. NNG 'BRIGHTMARK KIRKMAN BIOGAS DEL', FGT 'Southern Cross Dairy RNG - FGT Delivery'): Flow Ind D rows are not injection capacity (9 of 24 NNG 'BIOGAS' rows on 2026-11-27).
Design/Operating Capacity at an existing RNG point is sized for that point; it says nothing about capacity for a new plant elsewhere on the pipeline.
OAC = what remains after scheduled quantities for that day and cycle; it changes every cycle and is an estimate ('no guarantees expressed or implied').
NNG CSV downloads end with 7 'Comments:' rows that are not data; filter rows without a Loc number.

Some FGT RNG receipt points are interconnects whose upstream party is an LDC (Peoples Gas System) and whose names end in '- PGS' or '- TECO' (Locations type INT/OTH): the capacity is that of the pipeline-to-LDC interconnect, not of the plant connection.
Position is county/state (NNG adds PLSS section-township-range); no coordinates: good for a county map, not for measuring distance to a plant.
Point counts grow over time (NNG 'BIOGAS' rows: 1 on 2020-11-27, 9 on 2023-11-27, 21 on 2025-11-27, 24 on 2026-11-27): a series per point starts at its effective date.

problems: Williams 1Line (Transco) and Enbridge infopost (Texas Eastern) return 403 to automated clients.
Kinder Morgan and TC Energy postings load data through ASP.NET postbacks or a JavaScript application; no plain URL to the point table was found.

sources.name: Gas utility (LDC) renewable gas interconnection screening and feasibility studies
sources.publisher: Local gas distribution utilities under state commission tariffs (sample: PG&E, SoCalGas, Con Edison, National Grid, NW Natural)
sources.format: Study report delivered to the applicant (PDF); procedures as web pages and tariff PDFs
sources.adds: The only route to capacity at a proposed location on distribution/utility networks: a per-project study reports the nearest pipe with takeaway capacity, its MAOP and pressures. Nothing is published as a map or table.
sources.summary: On distribution and utility networks, capacity at a proposed location is given only in a per-project screening/feasibility study requested by the developer.
sources.coverage_note: PG&E and SoCalGas follow the CPUC standard tariff (free screening, 15 business days); Con Edison, National Grid and NW Natural run similar request-based reviews.
caveats: Study results are non-binding, project-specific and not public.
Summer low-demand hours limit distribution takeaway (SoCalGas).

coverage.geographic: Per utility service territory; California investor-owned gas utilities share one standard tariff (D.20-08-035); New York and Oregon utilities checked.

unit.value: MScfd / MMScfd (thousand / million standard cubic feet per day) in the California standard tariff; the developer's fact sheet uses Scf/h and MScf/d.
unit.quote: Thousand Standard cubic feet per day (MScfd or MScf/d) Volumetric flow of Gas measured in thousands of standard cubic feet per day.

attempts.note: Same definition in the tariff adopted by D.20-08-035.

inclusion_rule.value: One study per proposed project and location, on written request with an interconnection fact sheet; first screening free in California.
inclusion_rule.quote: Any Renewable Gas Interconnector, including an interconnecting pipeline or a supply source, may request one displacement Interconnection Screening for each project, free of charge.

reference_date.value: Date of each study report (delivered within 15 business days for California screenings); no public dated release exists.
reference_date.quote: The report shall be provided by the Utility within fifteen (15) business days of its receipt of a written request and complete interconnection fact sheet.

attempts.note: Procedure page describes studies on request; no publication schedule.
Tariff sets study deadlines, not periodic publication.

exclusions.value: Capacity is preliminary and non-binding, set solely by the utility, and varies daily with other receipts, storage and end-use demand; summer low-demand hours limit distribution takeaway.
exclusions.quote: Takeaway Capacity for any particular day may be affected by physical flows from other Receipt Points, physical pipeline and/or storage conditions for that Day, and end-use demand on the Utility's pipeline system, and will be solely determined by the Utility.

attempts.note: SoCalGas 2017: 'Majority of the pipelines in streets are distribution lines with limited takeaway capability to accept interconnector gas during summer months (particularly in the early a.m. hours)'.

key_fields.meaning: Utility's physical capability downstream of the interconnection point; determined per study, not published.
Metering, regulation and odorization capacity of the receipt point; explicitly not a commitment of takeaway capacity.
Receipt capacity on a given day, affected by other receipts, storage and demand.
Maximum allowable and normal operating pressure of the candidate pipe, reported in the PG&E screening study.

how_to_use.example_result: PG&E Interconnection Screening Study provides: 'Location of the nearest gas pipe system that can accommodate the supply volume without restriction'; 'Maximum Allowable Operating Pressure (MAOP) and Normal Operating Pressure (NOP) of that gas pipe system'; 'The takeaway capacity of the pipe system closest to the upgrading facilities'. Allow up to 15 business days; no cost.
steps: PG&E: the screening study is requested with the Renewable Gas Interconnect Fact Sheet (Form 79-1210), which asks for forecasted maximum/minimum flow in Scf/h and whether operation is seasonal.
The Preliminary Engineering Study (PG&E: $50K, up to 90 business days) confirms 'that the identified pipe can receive the proposed supply 24X7'.

Con Edison (NY): an application with fee starts an Initial Feasibility Review that identifies the interconnection location, operating pressures and takeaway capacity; only 15-99 psi high-pressure distribution mains are eligible.
NW Natural (OR/WA): an RNG Producer Inquiry Form starts the initial evaluation of a project's potential connection.
reading_traps: A study value describes one project at one location and date; it is not a published available capacity for others.
Interconnect (meter) capacity is not takeaway capacity of the network.
A pipe near the site may lack capacity: SoCalGas warns 'Existence of a gas line does not mean it has the necessary capacity!'

problems: socalgas.com and nationalgrid.com reject automated clients (403 challenge page).
Study reports are delivered to applicants only; no public copy found.

if_unstructured.summary: Utility-network capacity is not published; public documents (CPUC biomethane reports, project cost cases) describe injected volumes or receipt-capacity upgrades without capacity values. The tested recipe compiles existing interstate RNG receipt-point capacity from postings.
recipe: For each interstate pipeline, open Informational Postings > Locations and filter or search biomethane points (NNG location type 'BIO'; FGT OAC location type 'RNG'; otherwise names containing RNG, BIOGAS, DAIRY). Tested on NNG (15 points) and FGT (5 receipt points).

Query Operationally Available Capacity for those Loc numbers and the gas day/cycle wanted; keep Flow Ind R rows; store Design Capacity, Operating Capacity, Total Scheduled Quantity and OAC with the Effective Gas Day and Post Date/Time.
Join on Loc to the Locations list for county, state, effective date and upstream party; drop the delivery (D) rows that share the site name.
Treat the result as capacity at existing points only; for utility networks no public figure exists and the value must come from the utility's screening study.
if_unstructured.location_method: Pipeline Locations lists give county and state (NNG also PLSS section-township-range); no coordinates were found in the postings.
cross_with: EPA LMOP project data to identify landfill RNG projects behind a receipt point (production, not capacity).
Utility procedure pages (PG&E, SoCalGas Rule 45, Con Edison) for points on LDC networks.
